boards.title: 10 Late-Night Runs That Explain Colorado School of Mines
boards.description: Build an under-21-safe late-night ritual board. Every card needs a currently verifiable destination, a direct source supporting late availability, and a conservative explanation of why it matters near this campus. Do not invent student habits, signature orders, popularity, or current hours. Bars and 21+-only venues are prohibited.

cards.title: Elements
cards.subtitle: Ben Parker Student Center
cards.notes: Visit this on-campus convenience store for late-night snacks, beverages, and a F'real milkshake machine. It serves as a primary hub for students studying in the student center.
cards.short_summary: Elements is a campus convenience store in the Ben Parker Student Center offering snacks and milkshakes until 10:00 PM.
cards.evidence_claim: Elements is open until 10:00 PM Monday through Thursday during the regular academic semester.
cards.source_title: Elements - Colorado School of Mines Dining
cards.access_notes: Open until 10:00 PM Monday-Thursday during regular semester hours.

cards.title: Qdoba Mexican Eats
cards.subtitle: Ben Parker Student Center
cards.notes: Head to the Periodic Table food court for late-night burritos and bowls. It is one of the few on-campus hot food options available after standard dinner hours.
cards.short_summary: Qdoba Mexican Eats is an on-campus retail dining option located in the Ben Parker Student Center food court.
cards.evidence_claim: Qdoba at the Periodic Table is open until 10:00 PM Monday through Thursday.
cards.source_title: Hours of Operation - Colorado School of Mines Dining
cards.access_notes: Retail hours extend to 10:00 PM Monday-Thursday.

cards.title: Woody's Wood-Fired Pizza
cards.subtitle: Washington Avenue
cards.notes: Stop by this Golden staple for wood-fired pizza and wings. The dining room remains open until 11:00 PM daily, making it a popular off-campus gathering spot.
cards.short_summary: Woody's Wood-Fired Pizza is a long-standing local restaurant in downtown Golden known for its pizza buffet and late hours.
cards.evidence_claim: Woody's Wood-Fired Pizza is open every day from 11:00 AM to 11:00 PM.
cards.source_title: Woody's Wood-Fired Pizza Restaurant - Golden, Colorado
cards.access_notes: Open until 11:00 PM daily for dine-in service.

cards.title: Safeway
cards.subtitle: Jackson Street
cards.notes: Walk to this grocery store near campus for late-night supplies or deli items. It is a frequent stop for students living in nearby residence halls or apartments.
cards.short_summary: Safeway is a full-service grocery store located within walking distance of the Colorado School of Mines campus.
cards.evidence_claim: The Safeway at 1701 Jackson St in Golden is open until 11:00 PM daily.
cards.source_title: Grocery Store Near Me - Safeway in Golden, CO
cards.access_notes: Store hours are 6:00 AM to 11:00 PM daily.

cards.title: Taco Bell
cards.subtitle: South Golden Road
cards.notes: Drive to South Golden Road for late-night tacos and burritos. The drive-thru remains open well past midnight, serving as a reliable option for late study sessions.
cards.short_summary: Taco Bell is a fast-food restaurant offering late-night drive-thru service near the Mines campus.
cards.evidence_claim: The Taco Bell at 17764 S Golden Rd is open until 3:00 AM on Thursdays and 4:00 AM on Fridays.
cards.source_title: Taco Bell in Golden, CO - 17764 S Golden Rd
cards.access_notes: Drive-thru open until 3:00 AM or 4:00 AM on most nights.

cards.title: McDonald's
cards.subtitle: South Golden Road
cards.notes: Visit this 24-hour drive-thru for classic fast food at any hour. It is one of the only truly 24/7 food options available to students in the Golden area.
cards.short_summary: McDonald's provides 24-hour drive-thru service on South Golden Road, catering to late-night student needs.
cards.evidence_claim: The McDonald's at 17500 S Golden Rd features a 24-hour drive-thru.
cards.source_title: Fast Food in Golden, CO at 17500 S Golden Rd | McDonald's
cards.access_notes: Drive-thru is open 24 hours daily.

cards.title: Moonlight Breakfast
cards.subtitle: Elm Hall
cards.notes: Attend this semesterly tradition during finals week for free late-night breakfast. It is a major campus event designed to provide a study break for all students.
cards.short_summary: Moonlight Breakfast is a recurring late-night event at Mines Market offering free food to students during finals.
cards.evidence_claim: Mines Market hosts Moonlight Breakfast from 8:00 PM to 9:30 PM during finals week, providing free meals to students with a Blaster Card.
cards.source_title: Moonlight Breakfast 2026 - Mines Daily Blast System
cards.access_notes: Event typically held from 8:00 PM to 9:30 PM; requires Blaster Card for entry.

cards.title: D.P. Dough
cards.subtitle: Delivery to Campus
cards.notes: Order late-night calzones for delivery to campus. While located in Denver, this chain is a staple for college students seeking food in the early morning hours.
cards.short_summary: D.P. Dough is a late-night calzone specialist that delivers to the Golden area and Mines campus.
cards.evidence_claim: D.P. Dough Denver is open and delivers until 2:00 AM or 3:00 AM most nights.
cards.source_title: DP Dough Denver
cards.access_notes: Delivery available until 2:00 AM (Sun-Thu) and 3:00 AM (Fri-Sat).

cards.title: Jimmy John's
cards.subtitle: Washington Avenue
cards.notes: Get a sandwich delivered fast or pick one up in downtown Golden. The central location makes it a convenient stop for students moving between campus and downtown.
cards.short_summary: Jimmy John's offers quick sandwich options with delivery and pickup service in downtown Golden.
cards.evidence_claim: The Jimmy John's at 1299 Washington Ave is open until 9:00 PM daily.
cards.source_title: Sandwich Shop & Gourmet Subs in Golden | Jimmy John's 1066
cards.access_notes: Open until 9:00 PM daily for pickup and delivery.

cards.title: South Table Market
cards.subtitle: Lookout Apartments
cards.notes: Use the Grubhub app to access this frictionless market for snacks and essentials. It provides a modern, tech-driven shopping experience for students on the south side of campus.
cards.short_summary: South Table Market is a frictionless, app-based convenience store located in the Lookout Apartments on campus.
cards.evidence_claim: South Table Market is a frictionless store where students enter using the Grubhub app to purchase snacks and meals.
cards.source_title: South Table Market - Colorado School of Mines Dining
cards.access_notes: Accessible via the Grubhub app; check app for current daily hours.

boards.title: What the Campus Tour Skips: 10 Places Students Share With Each Other
boards.description: Discover the functional study hubs and social nooks where Mines students actually spend their time between rigorous engineering labs and lectures.

cards.title: Arthur Lakes Library Map Room
cards.subtitle: Quiet Study in the Library
cards.notes: Visit the 2nd floor for a quiet atmosphere surrounded by the library's extensive map collection. It is a preferred spot for students seeking minimal distractions.
cards.short_summary: A quiet, specialized study area within the main campus library featuring large tables and map collections.
cards.evidence_claim: The map room is noted by students as a quiet and underutilized study space within the Arthur Lakes Library.
cards.source_title: Study and Meeting Rooms - Arthur Lakes Library
cards.access_notes: Open during regular library hours; accessible to all students with a valid BlasterCard.

cards.title: CoorsTek Center Upper Floors
cards.subtitle: Modern Collaborative Spaces
cards.notes: Head to the 2nd and 3rd floors for open collaborative seating and natural light. These areas are often less crowded than the ground floor lobby.
cards.short_summary: Modern, light-filled collaborative study areas located on the upper levels of the CoorsTek Center.
cards.evidence_claim: The upper floors of CoorsTek are identified as underutilized spaces with a variety of collaborative and individual seating options.
cards.source_title: Self-Guided Walking Tour - Colorado School of Mines
cards.access_notes: Accessible during building hours, typically 7:00 AM to 10:00 PM on weekdays.

cards.title: Marquez Hall Reflection Space
cards.subtitle: Quiet Room 223
cards.notes: Find Room 223 on the second floor for a carpeted, quiet space intended for prayer, meditation, or a brief mental break from engineering coursework.
cards.short_summary: A dedicated quiet room in Marquez Hall designed for reflection, prayer, and stress reduction.
cards.evidence_claim: Marquez Hall Room 223 is a designated reflection space open to all of campus for quiet time and meditation.
cards.source_title: MZ now has reflection space in room 223 - Mines Daily Blast
cards.access_notes: Open during Marquez Hall building hours; available to all students and staff.

cards.title: Brown Hall Conversation Nooks
cards.subtitle: Engineering Discourse Spaces
cards.notes: Utilize the small seating alcoves throughout the building for quick group huddles or individual work between labs in the Engineering Division.
cards.short_summary: Small, integrated seating areas within Brown Hall designed to encourage spontaneous academic discourse.
cards.evidence_claim: Brown Hall features conversation nooks and galleries specifically designed to encourage discourse among engineering students.
cards.source_title: Brown Hall Addition and Renovation - AMD Architects
cards.access_notes: Publicly accessible within the building during academic hours.

cards.title: McNeil Hall Collaboration Classrooms
cards.subtitle: After-Hours Study Hub
cards.notes: Check for empty classrooms after 3:00 PM. These rooms feature writable walls and multiple screens, making them ideal for group project sessions.
cards.short_summary: Modern classrooms in McNeil Hall that serve as high-tech group study spaces when not in use for instruction.
cards.evidence_claim: McNeil Hall classrooms are designed for collaboration with writable walls and are often used by students for study after 3 PM.
cards.source_title: McNeil Hall - OZ Architecture
cards.access_notes: Classrooms are generally available for student use when not scheduled for classes.

cards.title: Spruce Hall Zen Garden
cards.subtitle: Outdoor Quiet Space
cards.notes: Relax in this intimate outdoor garden located on the first floor of Spruce Hall. It is designed specifically for students seeking a low-stimulus environment.
cards.short_summary: A tranquil outdoor garden space at Spruce Hall designed for relaxation and quiet reflection.
cards.evidence_claim: Spruce Hall includes an intimate Zen garden and outdoor spaces designed for students sensitive to stimuli.
cards.source_title: Colorado School of Mines Spruce Residence Hall - NAC Architecture
cards.access_notes: Accessible to the campus community via the Spruce Hall first-floor public areas.

cards.title: Green Center Grand Lobby
cards.subtitle: WiFi-Friendly Exhibit Area
cards.notes: Use the large open lobby for casual study or meeting friends. The space is WiFi-friendly and often hosts campus exhibitions and trade shows.
cards.short_summary: A large, open public lobby in the Green Center used for both events and informal student study.
cards.evidence_claim: The Green Center Grand Lobby is a WiFi-friendly environment with over 7,000 square feet of open area for exhibits and study.
cards.source_title: Green Center Lobby and Exhibit Area - Colorado School of Mines
cards.access_notes: Open during building hours; typically used for large-scale campus events but available for seating otherwise.

cards.title: Starzer Welcome Center Heritage Lounge
cards.subtitle: Alumni and Visitor Gateway
cards.notes: Stop by this lounge at the corner of 19th and Illinois. While it serves as a gateway for visitors, it offers a comfortable, high-quality seating area on campus.
cards.short_summary: A well-appointed lounge in the Starzer Welcome Center used for welcoming the Mines community.
cards.evidence_claim: The Heritage Lounge in the Starzer Welcome Center is a major donor-funded space designed to welcome students, alumni, and visitors.
cards.source_title: From Stratton Hall to Starzer Welcome Center - Mines Newsroom
cards.access_notes: Open Monday through Friday, 8:00 AM to 5:00 PM.

cards.title: Alderson Hall Top Floor Desks
cards.subtitle: Traditional Academic Vibe
cards.notes: Seek out the desks at the ends of the hallways on the top floor for a quiet, traditional study environment with minimal foot traffic.
cards.short_summary: Quiet, individual study desks located in the upper hallways of Alderson Hall.
cards.evidence_claim: End-of-hall desks in Alderson Hall, particularly on the top floor, are popular for students preferring minimal distractions.
cards.source_title: Best Study Spots: Mines - Untapped Learning
cards.access_notes: Accessible during standard building hours for academic facilities.

cards.title: Elm Hall Community Kitchenette
cards.subtitle: Student Resource Hub
cards.notes: Use the community kitchenette to heat up lunch or take a break. It is one of several campus resources mapped for student daily use.
cards.short_summary: A functional community space in Elm Hall providing essential resources for students on campus.
cards.evidence_claim: Elm Hall is listed as a location for community kitchenettes and other useful resources for the Mines community.
cards.source_title: Every Oredigger Campus Resources Map - Colorado School of Mines
cards.access_notes: Primarily for residents, but listed as a campus resource for the broader Mines community.

boards.title: Zero Dollars: 10 Hangs That Cost Nothing
boards.description: Discover free social spaces and activities around the Colorado School of Mines campus, from world-class mineral museums to outdoor river trails and historic landmarks.

cards.title: Explore the Mineral Collection
cards.subtitle: 1310 Maple St, Golden, CO
cards.notes: Walk through an indoor cave and view a moon rock from Apollo 17. Admission is free for all visitors daily from 10 AM to 4 PM.
cards.short_summary: A free campus museum featuring over 3,000 minerals, fossils, and gemstones on display.
cards.evidence_claim: Admission is FREE. Regular Hours: DAILY 10AM- 4PM. Location: Colorado School of Mines, General Research Lab (GRL) building, 1310 Maple St.
cards.source_title: Mines Museum of Earth Science - Colorado School of Mines
cards.access_notes: Open daily 10 AM - 4 PM; closed on major holidays.

cards.title: Watch the Kayakers
cards.subtitle: 1201 10th St, Golden, CO
cards.notes: Relax by the banks of Clear Creek to watch kayakers and tubers navigate the rapids. Public access is free and open from dawn to dusk.
cards.short_summary: A popular recreational area for whitewater sports and riverside lounging near campus.
cards.evidence_claim: There are no fees for drop-in usage. The course is divided into three sections spanning about 7 city blocks.
cards.source_title: Clear Creek Whitewater Park - City of Golden, Colorado
cards.access_notes: Open dawn to dusk; unsupervised recreational area.

cards.title: Study in the Open Stacks
cards.subtitle: 1400 Illinois St, Golden, CO
cards.notes: Find a quiet nook or join a group study session in the heart of campus. The library is open to the public for on-site research.
cards.short_summary: The primary academic library at Mines, offering public access to collections and study spaces.
cards.evidence_claim: Although the library is open to the public, the Mines community has priority access. Public access computers are available to search collections on site.
cards.source_title: User Access - Arthur Lakes Library - Colorado School of Mines
cards.access_notes: Public access is available during regular operating hours; check website for current schedule.

cards.title: Learn Local History
cards.subtitle: 923 10th St, Golden, CO
cards.notes: Explore exhibits on Golden's brewing history and legendary residents. Admission is always free for the public.
cards.short_summary: A city-run museum documenting the history and culture of Golden, Colorado.
cards.evidence_claim: Admission is always free. Open Tuesday – Saturday, 10 – 4:30.
cards.source_title: History Museum in Golden, Colo.
cards.access_notes: Open Tuesday through Saturday, 10 AM to 4:30 PM.

cards.title: Spot Dinosaur Tracks
cards.subtitle: 6th Ave & 19th St, Golden, CO
cards.notes: Hike this 1.5-mile gravel trail to see 68-million-year-old dinosaur tracks and plant impressions in old clay pits.
cards.short_summary: A self-guided geologic trail featuring fossilized tracks and prehistoric history.
cards.evidence_claim: Triceratops Trail is a 1.5-mile, gravel hiking trail... Admission is free year round.
cards.source_title: Triceratops Trail - Dinosaur Ridge
cards.access_notes: Open daily from sunrise to sunset.

cards.title: Hike the Nature Preserve
cards.subtitle: 910 Colorow Rd, Golden, CO
cards.notes: Explore interactive exhibits on the foothills ecosystem and hike trails with panoramic views of the Rockies.
cards.short_summary: A nature preserve and education center offering free admission and naturalist-led programs.
cards.evidence_claim: General Information: Family-Friendly, Free Admission. The Preserve is open daily from 8:00 am to dusk.
cards.source_title: Lookout Mountain Preserve and Nature Center
cards.access_notes: Nature Center open Friday-Monday 10 AM - 4 PM; Preserve open daily 8 AM to dusk.

cards.title: Hang Out on the Green
cards.subtitle: 1500 Illinois St, Golden, CO
cards.notes: The central green space on campus for student gatherings, outdoor studying, and major university events like Celebration of Mines.
cards.short_summary: The primary outdoor social hub and quad for the Colorado School of Mines community.
cards.evidence_claim: Kafadar Commons was covered with tents and booths... for the more than 100 student organizations on campus.
cards.source_title: Student groups turn out for Celebration of Mines
cards.access_notes: Publicly accessible outdoor campus space.

cards.title: Ride the Free Shuttle
cards.subtitle: Golden, CO
cards.notes: Use the free shuttle service to travel between campus, downtown Golden, and the RTD Light Rail station.
cards.short_summary: A free transit partnership between the university and the City of Golden for students and the public.
cards.evidence_claim: Operated as a partnership between Mines and the City of Golden and is free for all riders.
cards.source_title: Golden Visitors Guide - Campus Tour
cards.access_notes: Check the TransLoc app or university website for current routes and schedules.

cards.title: Start a Self-Guided Tour
cards.subtitle: 1812 Illinois St, Golden, CO
cards.notes: Pick up a map at the campus gateway to begin a one-mile walking tour of the historic university grounds.
cards.short_summary: The official campus gateway housing admissions and alumni services.
cards.evidence_claim: This one-mile walking tour begins at the Starzer Welcome Center, home to the Admissions Office.
cards.source_title: Self-Guided Walking Tour - Campus Tour
cards.access_notes: Open during business hours for visitors and prospective students.

cards.title: Visit the Student Plaza
cards.subtitle: Maple St, Golden, CO
cards.notes: A designated public speech and tabling area between the Student Center and Rec Center, ideal for people-watching and campus activity.
cards.short_summary: A central pedestrian plaza used for student organization tabling and public speech activities.
cards.evidence_claim: Public speech activities such as tabling are designated to take place on Maple Plaza, which is located between the Ben Parker Student Center & Student Recreation Center.
cards.source_title: Request for Mines Facility Use for Public Speech Activities
cards.access_notes: Publicly accessible outdoor pedestrian area.

boards.title: Claimed by 9am: 10 Study Spots Worth Showing Up Early For
boards.description: From high-tech collaborative labs to quiet traditional library nooks, these are the most reliable environments for focused work on the Mines campus.

cards.title: Reservable Study Rooms
cards.subtitle: Arthur Lakes Library
cards.notes: Book one of 11 reservable rooms for up to 3 hours daily. Most include whiteboards and lab computers for complex engineering problems.
cards.short_summary: The primary campus library offers 11 reservable rooms, including five dedicated specifically for graduate students.
cards.evidence_claim: The Arthur Lakes Library has 11 reservable study rooms; 7 small study rooms, 5 small Graduate Only student rooms, and 1 large study room.
cards.source_title: Study and Meeting Rooms - Arthur Lakes Library
cards.access_notes: Reservations are required through the library's online portal; rooms are for Mines community members only.

cards.title: Level 1 Collaborative Seating
cards.subtitle: CoorsTek Center for Applied Science and Engineering
cards.notes: Utilize flexible, media-intensive seating areas on the first floor. The glazed facade provides natural light and views of Kafadar Commons.
cards.short_summary: A modern facility featuring open, collaborative workspaces and active learning rooms designed for group projects.
cards.evidence_claim: Multiple entrances aligned with campus circulation paths invite the community into a welcoming public space with a variety of collaborative and individual seating options.
cards.source_title: CoorsTek Center for Applied Science and Engineering - Anderson Mason Dale Architects
cards.access_notes: Public seating areas on Level 1 are accessible during building hours; upper floors house specialized labs.

cards.title: Room 223 Reflection Space
cards.subtitle: Marquez Hall
cards.notes: Visit this carpeted quiet zone on the second floor for low-stress reflection or individual study. Follow posted rules for shared use.
cards.short_summary: A dedicated quiet room on the second floor of Marquez Hall intended for prayer, reflection, and silent study.
cards.evidence_claim: MZ now has reflection space in room 223 which is open to all of campus... located in room 223 on the second floor of Marquez Hall.
cards.source_title: MZ now has reflection space in room 223 which is open to all of campus - Mines Daily Blast
cards.access_notes: Open during standard Marquez Hall building hours; available to all campus members.

cards.title: Top Floor End-of-Hall Desks
cards.subtitle: Alderson Hall
cards.notes: Seek out the desks at the ends of the hallways on the 4th floor for a traditional, quiet academic atmosphere with minimal foot traffic.
cards.short_summary: Quiet, isolated desks located at the ends of hallways, particularly on the upper floors of Alderson Hall.
cards.evidence_claim: The end-of-hall desks, particularly on the top floor, are popular among students who prefer minimal distractions.
cards.source_title: Best Study Spots: Mines - Untapped Learning
cards.access_notes: Open access during building hours; desks are first-come, first-served.

cards.title: Academic Porch & Nooks
cards.subtitle: Brown Hall Addition
cards.notes: Study in the 'conversation nooks' or along the architectural porch that connects the building's interior to the pedestrian promenade.
cards.short_summary: A collaborative building featuring glass-walled labs, conversation nooks, and a porch area for academic discourse.
cards.evidence_claim: The project includes... conversation nooks and galleries for encouraging discourse... and an architectural porch.
cards.source_title: Brown Hall Addition and Renovation - Anderson Mason Dale Architects
cards.access_notes: Public areas and nooks are accessible during building hours; some labs require specific department access.

cards.title: Write-on Wall Classrooms
cards.subtitle: McNeil Hall
cards.notes: Use classrooms after 3pm for group work. These spaces feature multiple display screens and walls designed for writing with dry-erase markers.
cards.short_summary: Modern classrooms in McNeil Hall designed for collaboration with writable walls and flexible furniture.
cards.evidence_claim: Classrooms are designed for collaboration, with multiple display screens, walls you can write on, and a modern aesthetic.
cards.source_title: McNeil Hall, Colorado School of Mines | OZ Architecture
cards.access_notes: Classrooms are often available for student study after scheduled classes conclude, typically after 3:00 PM.

cards.title: Grand Lobby Seating
cards.subtitle: Cecil H. & Ida Green Graduate and Professional Center
cards.notes: Find a spot in the 7,000-square-foot open lobby. This WiFi-friendly environment is ideal for casual study between events.
cards.short_summary: A large, open exhibit area and lobby that serves as a WiFi-enabled space for student study and meetings.
cards.evidence_claim: Green Center contains more than 7,000 square feet of open area... Grand Lobby with measurements. WiFi Friendly Environment.
cards.source_title: Green Center Lobby and Exhibit Area - Colorado School of Mines
cards.access_notes: Accessible during building hours, though availability may be limited during major conferences or banquets.

cards.title: Main Lobby Lounge
cards.subtitle: Starzer Welcome Center
cards.notes: Study in the sophisticated lobby featuring granite accents and a campus timeline. It serves as a quiet gateway on the edge of campus.
cards.short_summary: The official campus gateway offering a professional and quiet lobby environment for visitors and students.
cards.evidence_claim: The main lobby welcomes guests with a strong back-lit granite logo... Leading into the additional spaces is a timeline.
cards.source_title: Colorado School of Mines, Starzer Welcome Center - Hord Coplan Macht
cards.access_notes: Open during standard business hours (typically 8am-5pm) as it houses the Admissions Office.

cards.title: Off-Peak Dining Booths
cards.subtitle: Elm Hall
cards.notes: Claim a booth during non-meal hours for a spacious workspace with strong WiFi. It is significantly less crowded between 2pm and 4pm.
cards.short_summary: The main dining hall provides large tables and booths that function as productive study spaces outside of peak meal times.
cards.evidence_claim: It's completely empty at off hours where you can claim a booth... the wifi is WAY better than the library.
cards.source_title: Study Spots : r/ColoradoSchoolOfMines
cards.access_notes: Entry typically requires a meal plan or door rate during operating hours; best for students already on campus dining plans.

cards.title: Geology Department Study Areas
cards.subtitle: Berthoud Hall
cards.notes: Find quiet corners near the Geology and Geological Engineering labs. This historic building offers a focused, low-distraction environment.
cards.short_summary: A central academic building housing geology labs and classrooms with various quiet nooks for individual study.
cards.evidence_claim: Berthoud is home to offices, labs, and classrooms for Geology and Geological Engineering... You'll also find study spaces.
cards.source_title: Academic Buildings - Campus Tour - Colorado School of Mines
cards.access_notes: Open during standard academic building hours; study areas are located throughout the hallways and near labs.

boards.title: 10 Blocks Off Campus, One Reason Each
boards.description: Explore the essential streets and corridors surrounding the Colorado School of Mines campus in Golden, featuring student-centric study spots, housing, and local landmarks.

cards.title: Downtown's Main Street
cards.subtitle: Washington Avenue Corridor
cards.notes: Walk under the iconic 'Welcome to Golden' arch and visit local boutiques and cafes just steps from the eastern edge of campus.
cards.short_summary: The primary commercial thoroughfare of downtown Golden, located adjacent to the Mines campus.
cards.evidence_claim: Washington Avenue is the heart of downtown Golden, featuring the 'Welcome to Golden' arch and numerous local shops and cafes within walking distance of campus.
cards.source_title: Historic Downtown Golden | Shops, Landmarks & Local Flavor
cards.access_notes: Public street accessible 24/7; business hours vary.

cards.title: Golden's Living Room
cards.subtitle: 13th Street Corridor
cards.notes: Visit Cafe 13 in the historic Armory building for a popular student study spot known for its breakfast and in-house bakery.
cards.short_summary: A key corridor housing the historic Armory building and popular student-frequented cafes.
cards.evidence_claim: Cafe 13 is located on 13th Street in the historic Armory building and is described as 'Golden's Living Room'.
cards.source_title: Cafe 13 - Golden
cards.access_notes: Cafe 13 open daily for breakfast and lunch.

cards.title: Sophomore Living Hub
cards.subtitle: Jackson Street Corridor
cards.notes: Head to 1750 Jackson for dedicated second-year student housing located conveniently near downtown businesses and Safeway.
cards.short_summary: A residential and commercial street featuring major university-owned sophomore housing.
cards.evidence_claim: 1750 Jackson is the university's first building dedicated to second-year undergraduate housing, located near downtown Golden.
cards.source_title: 1750 Jackson - Residence Life
cards.access_notes: Residential building access limited to students; street is public.

cards.title: Coffee and Community
cards.subtitle: 14th Street Corridor
cards.notes: Stop by Higher Grounds Cafe at the corner of 14th and Washington for organic coffee and a dedicated student-friendly atmosphere.
cards.short_summary: A downtown street corner home to a long-standing cafe serving the Mines community.
cards.evidence_claim: Higher Grounds Cafe is located at 14th and Washington and has served the Colorado School of Mines for over 20 years.
cards.source_title: Higher Grounds Cafe Golden
cards.access_notes: Open daily from 6 AM to 6:30 PM.

cards.title: Historic Food Hall
cards.subtitle: Ford Street Corridor
cards.notes: Gather at The Golden Mill for diverse food stalls and rooftop views of Clear Creek in a converted historic flour mill.
cards.short_summary: A street featuring a prominent community food hall and historic landmarks.
cards.evidence_claim: The Golden Mill is a food hall located at 1012 Ford Street in a historic former flour mill.
cards.source_title: The Golden Mill | Home
cards.access_notes: Open daily from 11 AM to 10 PM.

cards.title: Retro Gear and History
cards.subtitle: 12th Street Corridor
cards.notes: Explore the historic 12th Street neighborhood and shop for retro-inspired outdoor apparel at YoColorado.
cards.short_summary: A historic residential and retail street known for its architecture and local brands.
cards.evidence_claim: YoColorado is located at 805 12th Street in the historic 12th Street neighborhood of Golden.
cards.source_title: YoColorado - Golden Chamber of Commerce
cards.access_notes: Retail hours typically 10 AM to 6 PM.

cards.title: Coworking and Collaboration
cards.subtitle: Arapahoe Street Corridor
cards.notes: Find flexible workspace and networking opportunities at Connects Workspace, located just behind Cafe 13.
cards.short_summary: A street housing professional coworking spaces and community non-profits.
cards.evidence_claim: Connects Workspace Golden is located at 1301 Arapahoe Street, offering coworking and meeting spaces.
cards.source_title: Golden — Connects Workspace
cards.access_notes: Business hours Monday-Friday 8 AM to 5 PM.

cards.title: Mines Park Gateway
cards.subtitle: 19th Street Corridor
cards.notes: Follow 19th Street west to reach Mines Park, a major apartment-style community for upper-division and graduate students.
cards.short_summary: The primary access road for the university's western residential complex and mountain trails.
cards.evidence_claim: The Village at Mines Park is located off 19th Street on the west side of U.S. 6.
cards.source_title: The Village at Mines Park - Residence Life
cards.access_notes: Public street; residential complex access for residents.

cards.title: Performing Arts Hub
cards.subtitle: Miners Alley Corridor
cards.notes: Discover local theater and performing arts classes at the Miners Alley Performing Arts Center in the heart of downtown.
cards.short_summary: A unique alleyway corridor home to Golden's premier professional theater company.
cards.evidence_claim: Miners Alley Performing Arts Center is located at 1101 Miners Alley in Golden.
cards.source_title: Miners Alley Performing Arts Center
cards.access_notes: Box office and performance hours vary by show.

cards.title: Clear Creek Access
cards.subtitle: 10th Street Corridor
cards.notes: Access the Clear Creek trail and Parfet Park from 10th Street for outdoor recreation and community events.
cards.short_summary: A northern downtown street providing direct access to Golden's parks and creek-side trails.
cards.evidence_claim: 10th Street provides access to Parfet Park and the Clear Creek trail system in downtown Golden.
cards.source_title: Parks & Trails - Golden, Colorado
cards.access_notes: Parks open daily from sunrise to sunset.

boards.title: Only Happens Here: 10 Traditions That Make No Sense Anywhere Else
boards.description: From hauling 10-pound rocks up a mountain to receiving diplomas made of solid silver, these traditions define the Oredigger experience at Colorado School of Mines.

cards.title: The M Climb
cards.subtitle: A 10-Pound Welcome to Campus
cards.notes: New students carry a 10-pound rock from their hometown up Mount Zion to add to the iconic 'M' and coat it in fresh whitewash.
cards.short_summary: An annual orientation ritual where freshmen hike Mount Zion with rocks to maintain the school's mountainside emblem.
cards.evidence_claim: The M Climb is a signature experience where first-year students carry a 10-pound rock from their hometown to add to the hillside 'M'.
cards.source_title: M Climb - Signature Experience
cards.access_notes: Occurs annually at the start of the fall semester; involves a steep hike up Mount Zion.

cards.title: Silver-Plated Diplomas
cards.subtitle: Heavy Metal Graduation
cards.notes: Since 1934, Mines graduates have received unique 5x5.75 inch silver-plated metal diplomas instead of traditional paper ones.
cards.short_summary: A long-standing tradition where graduates receive an official university diploma engraved on a silver-plated metal sheet.
cards.evidence_claim: All Mines graduates receive one silver-plated metal diploma for each degree awarded as their official university diploma.
cards.source_title: 90 years of the Mines Silver Diploma - Mines Foundation
cards.access_notes: Awarded to all students upon successful completion of their degree requirements.

cards.title: The Ore Cart Pull
cards.subtitle: Hauling History to the Capitol
cards.notes: During E-Days, students pull a 200-pound ore cart over 7 miles from the Golden campus to the Colorado State Capitol in Denver.
cards.short_summary: A grueling spring tradition where Orediggers manually transport a mining cart to the state capitol building.
cards.evidence_claim: The Ore Cart Pull involves students pulling a 200-pound ore cart from Golden to the state capitol building in Denver.
cards.source_title: E-Days - Signature Experience
cards.access_notes: Takes place on the Friday of Engineering Days (E-Days) each April.

cards.title: Cardboard Boat Race
cards.subtitle: Engineering vs. Clear Creek
cards.notes: Teams build vessels using only cardboard and duct tape to navigate the rapids of Clear Creek during the annual E-Days festival.
cards.short_summary: A competitive engineering challenge where students race homemade cardboard boats down the local river.
cards.evidence_claim: The Cardboard Boat Race features nearly 100 student teams testing cardboard creations in the waters of Clear Creek.
cards.source_title: Inside the Cardboard Boat Race at Mines
cards.access_notes: Held at Clear Creek in Golden; open to public spectators every April.

cards.title: Blaster the Burro
cards.subtitle: The Hardest Working Mascot
cards.notes: A live burro named Blaster leads the football team onto the field and sprints across the end zone after every Oredigger touchdown.
cards.short_summary: The school's live mascot, a burro that performs celebratory runs during home football games.
cards.evidence_claim: Blaster the Burro is a live mascot who leads the football team and races around after every touchdown.
cards.source_title: Mines Traditions - Blaster
cards.access_notes: Visible at home football games at Marv Kay Stadium.

cards.title: The Mines Hat
cards.subtitle: A Branded Senior Sendoff
cards.notes: Revived for the 150th anniversary, seniors receive Western-style hats which they can have custom-branded during graduation week.
cards.short_summary: A modern revival of the 'Senior Stetson' tradition where graduates wear and brand specific Western hats.
cards.evidence_claim: The Mines Hat tradition involves graduating students receiving and branding Western-style hats to honor their heritage.
cards.source_title: Mines Hat - Commencement
cards.access_notes: Branding events occur during senior week and commencement festivities.

cards.title: The Mining Engineer
cards.subtitle: The 'Helluva' Fight Song
cards.notes: Orediggers sing this 1870s-era fight song, proudly claiming it predates Georgia Tech's similar 'Ramblin' Wreck' version.
cards.short_summary: The university's historic fight song, known for its repetitive 'helluva engineer' chorus.
cards.evidence_claim: The Mines fight song, 'The Mining Engineer', dates back to the 1870s and predates Georgia Tech's version by over 30 years.
cards.source_title: The Mines Fight Song - Athletics
cards.access_notes: Sung at all athletic events and during the M Climb.

cards.title: E-Days Fireworks
cards.subtitle: Golden's Biggest Light Show
cards.notes: The Engineering Days festival concludes with a massive aerial fireworks display that is visible across the entire Denver metro area.
cards.short_summary: A signature pyrotechnic show that serves as the grand finale for the annual spring E-Days celebration.
cards.evidence_claim: E-Days features one of the best fireworks shows around, which is an all-aerial display visible from many areas of Golden.
cards.source_title: Mines E-Days April 16-18, 2026
cards.access_notes: Typically starts at 9:05 PM on the Saturday of E-Days; best viewed from the North IM Field.

cards.title: Whitewashing the M
cards.subtitle: A Fresh Coat for the Mountain
cards.notes: Students use buckets of white paint to refresh the 104-foot by 107-foot mountainside emblem, often getting more paint on themselves than the rocks.
cards.short_summary: The physical maintenance part of the M Climb where students apply white paint to the hillside monument.
cards.evidence_claim: Students participate in throwing buckets of fresh white paint on the rocks of the M during the annual climb.
cards.source_title: The M Climb - Mines Foundation
cards.access_notes: Occurs during the M Climb; participants are advised to wear clothes they don't mind getting painted.

cards.title: Lighting of the M
cards.subtitle: A Beacon Over Golden
cards.notes: The Blue Key Honor Society maintains the M's lighting system, occasionally changing the LED colors to red hearts for Valentine's Day or patriotic themes.
cards.short_summary: The tradition of illuminating the mountainside 'M' with specific colors or patterns for holidays and events.
cards.evidence_claim: The M is maintained by Mines' Blue Key club and is occasionally lit in custom designs like red hearts for Valentine's Day.
cards.source_title: How Mines students turned the iconic 'M' into a Valentine's heart
cards.access_notes: The M is lit nightly; special designs are visible from across the city on specific holidays.

boards.title: Your First Weekend at Colorado School of Mines, Shared as Cards
boards.description: Build a plausible under-21-safe first-weekend sequence, not a ranking. Give each card one role in the sequence and use evergreen places or recurring behaviors rather than one-time events. Be conservative about hours, access, and travel time unless directly sourced.

cards.title: Check In at the Gateway
cards.subtitle: 1812 Illinois St, Golden, CO 80401
cards.notes: Start your journey at this modern hub for admissions and alumni. It serves as the official entry point for new Orediggers and their families during move-in weekend.
cards.short_summary: The official welcome center and starting point for new students at Colorado School of Mines.
cards.evidence_claim: The Starzer Welcome Center is the home for the Office of Admissions and serves as a primary campus tour and welcome starting point.
cards.source_title: From Stratton Hall to Starzer Welcome Center
cards.access_notes: Open during standard business hours; extended hours often apply during orientation weekends.

cards.title: Attend University Convocation
cards.subtitle: Inside the Student Recreation Center
cards.notes: Gather with your entire class for the official welcome ceremony. This formal induction marks the beginning of your academic career at Mines.
cards.short_summary: The venue for the official Mines welcome ceremony for all new students and their families.
cards.evidence_claim: Convocation is the official Mines welcome ceremony held in Lockridge Arena inside the Student Recreation Center.
cards.source_title: Helluva Welcome - New Student and Transition Services
cards.access_notes: Tickets are required for guests; students do not need tickets for this specific event.

cards.title: Join the Welcome BBQ
cards.subtitle: Central Campus Green Space
cards.notes: Head to the campus green for a community meal after convocation. It is a prime spot to meet fellow first-years and their families in a relaxed setting.
cards.short_summary: A central campus lawn used for major student gatherings, including the annual Welcome BBQ.
cards.evidence_claim: The New Student & Family Welcome BBQ is held at Kafadar Commons following the convocation ceremony.
cards.source_title: New Student & Family Welcome BBQ - Mines Events
cards.access_notes: Open to new students and their families during orientation; typically held in the early evening.

cards.title: Participate in the M Climb
cards.subtitle: Hike to the Iconic 'M'
cards.notes: Carry a 10-pound rock from your hometown up Mount Zion to help whitewash the 'M'. This century-old tradition is a rite of passage for every Oredigger.
cards.short_summary: A signature Mines tradition where freshmen hike Mount Zion to maintain the university's hillside emblem.
cards.evidence_claim: The M Climb is a symbolic initiation where students carry a 10-pound rock from their hometown to place on the 'M' on Mount Zion.
cards.source_title: The History of the M Climb
cards.access_notes: The climb is a scheduled orientation event; the trail itself is open from sunrise to sundown.

cards.title: Explore the Geology Museum
cards.subtitle: 1310 Maple St, Golden, CO 80401
cards.notes: See moon rocks and glowing minerals at one of the top earth science museums in the country. It is a quiet, fascinating way to spend a weekend afternoon.
cards.short_summary: A world-class geology museum on campus featuring minerals, fossils, and gemstones.
cards.evidence_claim: The Mines Museum of Earth Science offers free admission and is open daily from 10 AM to 4 PM.
cards.source_title: Mines Museum of Earth Science
cards.access_notes: Admission is free for all visitors; open daily 10am-4pm.

cards.title: Visit the Rec Center
cards.subtitle: 1651 Elm St, Golden, CO 80401
cards.notes: Check out the climbing wall or the elevated jogging track. It is the primary hub for fitness and intramural sports on campus.
cards.short_summary: The main campus facility for fitness, swimming, and indoor recreation.
cards.evidence_claim: The Student Recreation Center features a 4,000 sq. ft. climbing wall and an elevated jogging track.
cards.source_title: Student Recreation Center - Facilities
cards.access_notes: Weekend hours are typically 9am-7pm during the fall semester.

cards.title: Find Your Study Spot
cards.subtitle: 1400 Illinois St, Golden, CO 80401
cards.notes: Scout out the best quiet corners or collaborative rooms before classes start. The library is the intellectual heart of the Mines campus.
cards.short_summary: The primary academic library at Mines, offering diverse study environments and resources.
cards.evidence_claim: Arthur Lakes Library provides reservable study rooms and is open on Saturdays from 10 AM to 5 PM.
cards.source_title: Library Calendars - Arthur Lakes Library
cards.access_notes: Open Saturdays 10am-5pm; closed on Sundays during summer/orientation transitions.

cards.title: Explore CoorsTek Center
cards.subtitle: 1523 Illinois St, Golden, CO 80401
cards.notes: Walk through this high-tech building to find open-concept study areas with great views. It is designed to mimic a modern professional engineering environment.
cards.short_summary: A modern academic building known for its collaborative workspaces and natural light.
cards.evidence_claim: The CoorsTek Center features open environments and up-to-date technology for group projects and individual study.
cards.source_title: Best Study Spots: Mines
cards.access_notes: Generally accessible to students with a BlasterCard; open areas are available during building hours.

cards.title: Grab a Meal at Mines Market
cards.subtitle: 1795 Elm St, Golden, CO 80401
cards.notes: Experience the main dining hall's various stations. It is the primary social and nutritional hub for residential students on the south side of campus.
cards.short_summary: The central residential dining facility at Colorado School of Mines.
cards.evidence_claim: Mines Market is the primary dining location on campus, located at 1795 Elm Street.
cards.source_title: Mines Market - Mines Dining
cards.access_notes: Open daily during the academic year; hours vary by meal period.

cards.title: Walk the Clear Creek Trail
cards.subtitle: Adjacent to Campus
cards.notes: Take a break from campus and walk along the creek that runs through Golden. It is a popular spot for students to relax and enjoy the Colorado outdoors.
cards.short_summary: A scenic paved trail following Clear Creek, located just steps from the Mines campus.
cards.evidence_claim: The Clear Creek Trail is a popular recreational path in Golden used by students for walking and biking.
cards.source_title: Walking & Hiking Trails in Golden
cards.access_notes: Public trail open daily from dawn to dusk.
